project.objective: Who were the parents of Wendel Weichel (b. 1912, d. 1980, Odessa, Saskatchewan) — in particular his mother, whom the tree does not name?

questions.question: Who was the mother of Wendel Weichel (born 1912, died 1980, Odessa, Saskatchewan)?
questions.rationale: The tree does not name Wendel Weichel's mother — this is the central unknown in the research objective. Odessa is in Biggar No. 347 Rural Municipality, Saskatchewan. Saskatchewan has mandatory civil vital registration from 1878; a birth registration for Wendel (b. 1912) should exist and would name his mother. Canadian census returns for 1916, 1921, and 1931 (Saskatchewan nominal census 1926 also available) would show Wendel in his parents' household. This question drives the core of the objective and is the logical first decomposition of the two-fact 'parents' objective.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All seven stop criteria met. Three independent sources from different institutional origins converge on Josephine Reiss Weichel (I1) as the mother of Wendel Weichel (G8Q5-BJ1): (1) Canada immigration manifest 1924 (src_003) documents Josephina Weichel, b.1891, from Selz near Odessa, Russia, immigrating to Odessa, Saskatchewan; (2) 1926 Prairie Provinces Census (src_004) places Windelin Weichel (b.1913 Russia, probable=Wendel) as child_1 in Jacob Weishel's household with wife Josefine Weishel — direct parentage assertion; (3) Find a Grave memorial (src_002) encodes maiden name Reiss for Josephine Weichel, buried Odessa, SK. Conflict c_001 (Jacob/Joseph name discrepancy) resolved: the 1931 census confirmed a separate Joseph Weichel household at Odessa, supporting the Hamburg agent's substitution error. Saskatchewan birth certificate for Wendel is a structural non-gap: he was born in 1912 in Russia (Selz/Odessa region), predating Canadian immigration by 12 years — no Saskatchewan civil registration can exist. The decisive original record (Selz Catholic baptism register) is in European church archives inaccessible through North American FamilySearch tools. External sites (eHealth SK, SaskHomesteads, LAC) skipped as outside autonomous FamilySearch session scope and documented accordingly. No unsearched accessible source is likely to name a different mother.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1926 Saskatchewan census (src_004) names Windelin Weichel (probable = G8Q5-BJ1 Wendel Weichel) as child_1 of Jacob Weishel and Josefine Weishel (I1). Assertion a_035 is the direct parentage link. Find a Grave (src_002) supplies the maiden name Reiss. A defensible answer is obtained: Josephine Reiss Weichel is the mother of Wendel Weichel.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. Searched all indexed FamilySearch collections available for Saskatchewan 1912-1931: censuses for 1916, 1921, 1926, and 1931; Canada immigration records 1919-1924; Saskatchewan Catholic church records; Saskatchewan probate (FamilySearch, collection 1918293); Find a Grave. FAN research executed (pli_009): sibling search in 1931 census and Catholic baptism records. External sites (eHealth SK vital statistics, SaskHomesteads.com, Library and Archives Canada homestead files, browse-only provincial films) are outside this session's tool scope and documented as skipped. Family arrived in Canada 1924; pre-1924 Canadian records structurally inapplicable.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The 1926 census is an original government enumeration record; the immigration manifest is an original primary document (manifest image consulted to correct the indexed destination error). No derivative substituted for an accessible original. The Saskatchewan Catholic church index returned nil — no original was bypassed. Browse-only provincial birth registration films could not be accessed and are documented; no surrogate derivative was substituted in their place.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Met. Three independent sources with different informants and institutional origins: (a) Canada immigration manifest 1924 — Cunard/Hamburg agent, government of Canada record (src_003); (b) 1926 Prairie Provinces Census — Canadian federal census enumerator, separate government institution (src_004); (c) Find a Grave memorial for Josephine Reiss Weichel — volunteer contributor, third-party database (src_002). Each source was created through a different process by a different informant. The manifest and census are not derivative of each other.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The 1926 Prairie Provinces Census (src_004) is an original record produced by Canadian federal census enumerators; household composition and relationships are primary information for the enumeration date. Assertion a_035 (Windelin Weichel is child of Josefine Weishel) is direct evidence of the mother-child relationship. The immigration manifest (src_003) is also original, with primary information for identity and origin.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. Conflict c_001 (husband named 'Joseph' on immigration manifest vs 'Jacob' in 1926 census) is resolved with status 'resolved' and preferred_assertion_id a_016. Five independent reasons support the resolution: census is the stronger source; Hamburg agent completed the manifest without Josephina's verification; a separate Joseph Weichel family (b.1882, wife Katherine b.1884) confirmed at Odessa in 1931 census (log_025) shows the name was a known community name the agent could have substituted; 'Jakob' and 'Joseph' share initial J and are common Catholic German names; no candidate 'Joseph Weichel' b.c.1890 with Josephina wife and matching children was found in any record. No other conflicts are open.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Saskatchewan civil registration began 1888 with slow uptake; however, Wendel was born in 1912 in Russia (Selz/Odessa region, Russian Empire) and immigrated to Canada only in 1924 — a Saskatchewan birth certificate cannot exist for him. The decisive original parentage record is a Selz Catholic baptism register held in European church archives, which is genuinely inaccessible through North American FamilySearch-based tools (not a privacy embargo, but an archival access limitation). Three independent Canadian records agree on Josephine Reiss Weichel as the mother. No alternative mother candidate has appeared in any searched record. No unsearched accessible record type for this jurisdiction and period is expected to name a different mother.

items.rationale: eHealth Saskatchewan birth certificate index is an external site not accessible in this autonomous FamilySearch-only session. Parentage of Wendel Weichel established through multiple corroborating FamilySearch records (1926 census, Find a Grave, immigration manifest). Could be pursued manually to obtain a certified birth certificate naming parents directly.

Canada 1921 Census, FamilySearch collection 5000285 (indexed + images, free). Wendel Weichel would be approximately age 9 in 1921 and should appear in his parents' household in Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan. The census names every household member and their relationship to the head, supplying both parents' given names. This is a parallel primary source: even if the birth registration is missing or illegible, the 1921 census directly names the household. Search for 'Weichel' in Saskatchewan; also try 'Weixel' and 'Weichsel'. The RM of Francis No. 127 is a useful geographic filter.

1916 Prairie Provinces Census (Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Alberta), FamilySearch collection 1529118 (indexed + images, free). Wendel would be approximately age 4 and in his parents' household. This census is closer in time to his 1912 birth and more likely to find both parents in the same household. Even if his name was recorded with a spelling variant, searching by surname 'Weichel' or 'Weixel' in Saskatchewan should locate the family. Also available on Ancestry (collection 1556) and MyHeritage.

Canada, Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records, 1846-1957, FamilySearch collection 2001071 (indexed, 40,494 records, free). The surname Weichel is German in origin; German-speaking settlers in southeastern Saskatchewan were commonly Catholic or Lutheran. A Catholic baptism record for Wendel (c.1912) would name both parents — father's name and mother's maiden name. If Catholic, the Archdiocese of Regina covered this area. Also search Ancestry collection 61499 (Saskatchewan Catholic Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1867-1932) as a cross-check. If no Catholic record is found, this increases the probability of Lutheran affiliation — see pli_008.

Parents' civil marriage record — a dedicated search per the record-type guide's parentage standard. A civil marriage registration in Saskatchewan would name the bride and groom directly; the bride's surname at marriage is the mother's name used in registration, and from 1899 the form includes names of parents of both bride and groom. Search eHealth Saskatchewan marriage index (genealogy.ehealthsask.ca) for a Weichel marriage before 1912. The date window assumes parents married before Wendel's 1912 birth; if immigration was recent, the marriage may have occurred in Germany/Russia/elsewhere first — but a Saskatchewan ceremony or registration is still expected if the couple arrived before 1912. Try 'Weichel', 'Weixel', 'Weichsel' as groom surname variants. This record supplies the mother's maiden name — the marriage record is not, by itself, evidence that Wendel is their child, but corroborates parentage established by census household or birth registration.

Browse-only provincial Saskatchewan vital statistics image films require manual image-by-image review not achievable via FamilySearch indexed search in this autonomous session. Parentage established through other records; skipping per GPS proportionality.

Canada 1931 Census, FamilySearch collection 5000196 (indexed + images, free). Wendel would be approximately age 19; he may still be in his parents' household or living nearby. Even if Wendel has moved out, searching for the Weichel household in Francis No. 127 would still find his parents and establish their identities. Useful cross-check of names found in 1921 and 1916 censuses.

Homestead records (SaskHomesteads and Library and Archives Canada homestead files) are external sites not accessible in this FamilySearch-only session. Could be pursued manually via LAC to find Jacob Weishel's homestead application naming family members.

Sibling FAN searches executed across 1931 Canada census and Saskatchewan Catholic church records. Key finding: a separate 'Household of Joseph Weichel' (head b.1882, wife Katherine b.1884) at Odessa, Francis No. 127, SK was confirmed in 1931 — a different family from our Jacob/Josephine, supporting the conflict c_001 resolution that the Hamburg agent substituted the known community name 'Joseph Weichel' for 'Jakob Weishel.' Jacob Weishel (b.1890) was not found in 1931 census under any recognizable variant. No sibling baptism records found in Saskatchewan Catholic church records.

Probate search for Weichel/Weishel in Saskatchewan on FamilySearch returned nil. No Saskatchewan probate records for this family are indexed on FamilySearch. Provincial Archives records not accessible via FamilySearch in this session.

1926 Prairie Provinces Census (collection 3005862) searched for Weichel surname in Saskatchewan. Top match: 'Windelin Weichel' born 1913 Russia, single, in household of 'Jacob Weishel' in Weyburn No. 67, Saskatchewan, immigration 1924 — matchScore 0.478, above threshold. This name is a plausible variant of 'Wendel.' Household also contains Peter (b.1919 Russia), Augina (b.1922 Germany), Katherina (b.1923 Germany), Barbara (b.1925 Saskatchewan) Weichel. All appear to be recent immigrants (1924) except Barbara, Saskatchewan-born. Need to read the full household record for parents' names and head's details. The household is indexed under 'Jacob Weishel' — head likely the father. Also found: 'Frank Weixl' (b.1888 Hungary, Melfort) — different family. No match at Odessa/Francis No. 127 under any Weichel variant.

Top result: Find a Grave Index entry for 'Stanley Weichel', buried at Odessa, Regina Census Division, Saskatchewan — born 26 August 1941, died 1 December 2000. This appears to be Wendel's son (b.1941) not his father. The tree person G8QR-SBM 'Stanley Weichel' listed as possible father needs re-evaluation — born 1941 he is more likely Wendel's SON. No other 'Stanley Weichel' found in Saskatchewan in census records.

CRITICAL FINDING: Search for Rosa Deis in Saskatchewan reveals: (1) Find a Grave: 'Rose K. Deis Weichel' buried at Odessa, Regina Census Division, Saskatchewan, born 6 March 1914, died 11 September 2007 — confirms Rosa K. Deis (tree person GQB7-212) married a Weichel and was buried at Odessa alongside Wendel. Born 1914, she is YOUNGER than Wendel (b.1912) by 2 years, confirming she is Wendel's WIFE, not his mother. (2) 1926 Prairie Provinces Census: 'Rosa Deis' (b.1914 Saskatchewan) in household of 'Stony Deis' at Weyburn No. 67, Saskatchewan — SAME census district as the Jacob Weishel/Windelin Weichel household. (3) 1931 Canada Census: 'Rosa Deis' (b.1914 Saskatchewan, German, R.C., single) in household of 'Stoney Deis'. (4) 1911 Canada Census: Anton Deis household, Qu'Appelle, Saskatchewan — contains Rosa Deis (b.Feb 1911 Saskatchewan) and Rosa Deis (b.May 1879 Hungary, married). The two Deis families (Stony Deis and Anton Deis) are likely related. Rosa K. Deis Weichel (b. March 6, 1914) was in the Stony Deis household in Weyburn No. 67 — the same district as the Weishel/Weichel family. This strongly supports a Windelin Weichel (Jacob/Josefine Weishel's son) = our Wendel Weichel identification, and that Rosa Deis later became his wife.

Find a Grave search for Wendel Weichel in Canada. Top match (score 0.897, already attached to G8Q5-BJ1): 'Wendel A. Weichel' buried at Odessa, Regina Census Division, Saskatchewan — born 18 October 1912, died 27 December 1980. Confirms our subject's full birth date and death date. CRITICAL: Find a Grave also contains 'Josephine Reiss Weichel' (score 3.89, Find a Grave Index, collection 2221801) buried at Odessa, born 7 September 1891, died 27 January 1974. Maiden name 'REISS'. Born 1891, 21 years older than Wendel (b.1912) — right age to be his mother. Also buried at Odessa alongside Wendel, Rose K. Deis Weichel, and Stanley Weichel. This strongly suggests Josephine Reiss is Wendel's mother. Also found: Immigration Records 1919-1924 — 'Josephina Weichel' b.1891 from 'Sely Near Odesea' (Selz near Odessa, Russia — Volga German colony), immigration 1924; and 'Josef Weichel' b.1903 destination Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan.

Search for 'Josefine Weichel' in Canada returned 1096 results. Key finds: (1) Find a Grave: 'Josephine Reiss Weichel' b.7 Sep 1891, d.27 Jan 1974, buried Odessa — maiden name REISS, confirming mother candidate. (2) Saskatchewan Cemetery Transcripts: 'Josephine Weichel' b.1891, d.1974 — same person. (3) Immigration 1919-1924: 'Josephina Weichel' b.1891 from 'Sely Near Odesea' (German colony near Odessa, Russia). (4) 1931 Census: 'Joseph Weichel' b.1882 at Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan — another Weichel family member in the Odessa community. (5) Sebastian Weichel household in 1911 Qu'Appelle census — earlier Weichel presence in Saskatchewan.

Canada Immigration Records 1919-1924: 'Josephina Weichel' b.1891, married, German, from 'Sely Near Odesea' (Selz, a German Catholic colony near Odessa, Russia/Ukraine), immigration 1924. Birth year (1891) matches 'Josephine Reiss Weichel' buried Odessa, SK (b.7 Sep 1891). Destination indexed as Wellburn, Ontario — may be a transcription error for Weyburn, Saskatchewan. This woman is almost certainly Josefine Weishel from the 1926 Saskatchewan census (wife of Jacob Weishel, mother of Windelin/Wendel). Her origin 'near Odessa' Russia explains why the family settled at Odessa, Saskatchewan.

Canada Immigration Records 1919-1924: 'Josef Weichel' b.1903, single, German, from Hamburg, immigration destination Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan. This is a Weichel man who specifically immigrated TO Odessa, SK in 1924 — the same community where Wendel Weichel and Josephine Reiss Weichel are buried. Likely a relative (possibly older brother of Wendel). Shows Weichel family connection to Odessa, SK community.

Broadened search — Weichel/Weishel in 1931 Saskatchewan census. Found a 'Household of Joseph Weichel' at Odessa, Francis No. 127, SK with head born 1882 Russia, wife Katherine born 1884. This is a DIFFERENT family from our Jacob (b.1890)/Josephine (b.1891). Children: Larence b.1913, Barbara b.1912, Rafield/Raphael b.1919, Emanuel b.1921, Peter b.1924 — ages/names do not match our I2-I5. Jacob Weishel (our subject) was not found in the top 20 results for 1931 census. Finding relevant to conflict c_001: a separate 'Joseph Weichel' was already established at Odessa, consistent with the Hamburg agent having confused the name.

Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records birth search for Weichel/Weishel. 7 results, none match our family: earliest is Philomena Weichel, christened 1904 at Balgonie (a different Weichel family established in Saskatchewan before 1904). No baptism records found for our subject's siblings (Peter b.1919, Augina b.1922, Katherina b.1923, Barbara b.1925).

Searched Canada 1931 census for Jacob Weishel/Weichel. 8 results — best match is 'Jacob Watchel' at South Battleford, b.1876 Russia (a different person, 14 years older). No match for our Jacob (b.1890) with Josephine at Odessa. Family appears not enumerated or recorded under unrecognizable spelling in 1931 census.
FamilySearch probate search for Weichel/Weishel in Saskatchewan returned nil. No Saskatchewan probate records for this family indexed on FamilySearch.

Record read of the 'Household of Joseph Weichel' 1931 Canada Census (head persona ARK). Full household confirmed: Joseph Weichel (b.1882, Russia, RC, Farm Laborer, Married) with wife Katherine Weichel (b.1884, Russia) and children Barbara (b.1912), Larence (b.1913), Rafield/Raphael (b.1919), Emanuel (b.1921), Peter (b.1924) — all at Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan. CRITICAL NEW FINDING: This household's immigration date is 1930 — meaning this Joseph Weichel was still in Russia in 1924 when Josephina Weichel's immigration manifest was written. Therefore the 'Joseph Weichel' on Josephina's 1924 manifest cannot be this person. This strongly corroborates the conflict c_001 resolution: the Hamburg Cunard agent's 'Joseph' was a recording error for our Jacob Weishel (b.1890), the only Weichel husband known to have been in Odessa SK in 1924.

conflicts.description: Immigration manifest (1924) names Josephina Weichel's husband as 'Joseph Weichel' (a_009 via manifest image). The 1926 Prairie Provinces Census names the household head as 'Jacob Weishel' (a_016). These could refer to the same man with a recording error (Hamburg agent may have misheard or miswritten Jakob as Joseph — Josephina herself could not read) or to two different men. Current evidence cannot resolve this definitively.
conflicts.independence_analysis: The immigration manifest (1924) and the 1926 census are independent sources separated by 2 years. Neither derives from the other.
conflicts.weighing_analysis: The census was completed by an enumerator visiting the household; the manifest was filled by a Cunard agent in Hamburg from oral information provided by Josephina (who could not read and could not verify the spelling). A transcription error on the manifest from 'Jakob' to 'Joseph' is plausible. However, a second marriage cannot be ruled out without corroborating evidence.
conflicts.resolution_rationale: Preferred: 'Jacob Weishel' from the 1926 Canada census (src_004). 'Joseph' on the 1924 Hamburg immigration manifest (src_003) is assessed as a recording error by the Cunard shipping agent for five converging reasons: (1) The 1926 census, a direct Canadian enumeration taken just two years after arrival, consistently names the household head 'Jacob Weishel' with wife Josefine (b.1891) and children whose birth years and birth places match those on the manifest exactly; (2) The manifest was completed by a Hamburg agent, not by Josephina herself, who could not verify the transcribed name; (3) A completely separate 'Joseph Weichel' household (head b.1882, wife Katherine b.1884 — documented in src_005, assertions a_060–a_086) resided at Odessa, Francis No. 127, SK — but critically, their immigration date was 1930 (a_064), meaning this Joseph Weichel was still in Russia in 1924 when Josephina's manifest was written. He cannot be the 'Joseph Weichel' named on her manifest; (4) 'Jakob' and 'Joseph' share the initial letter J and are both common Catholic German names, consistent with a phonetic or common-name substitution error; (5) No candidate named 'Joseph Weichel' born c.1890 with wife 'Josephina' b.1891 and the same set of children has been found in any record. Confidence: probable — the census is the stronger source, the agent's error is well-motivated, and the 1930-immigration finding eliminates the only other 'Joseph Weichel' in the Odessa Volga-German community.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: Searched all indexed FamilySearch collections relevant to Saskatchewan 1912–1931: Canada Prairie Provinces Census 1926 (collection 3005862); Canada Immigration Records 1919–1924; Find a Grave Index for both Wendel A. Weichel and Josephine Reiss Weichel; Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records (collection 2001071, returned no record for the family); Saskatchewan probate (collection 1918293). FAN research executed: sibling search in the 1931 census confirmed a separate Joseph Weichel household at Odessa (b. 1882, wife Katherine b. 1884) consistent with the conflict resolution. The decisive original record — the Selz (Kutschurgan colony) Catholic baptism register held in European church archives — is genuinely inaccessible through North American FamilySearch tools, not a privacy embargo. Wendel Weichel was born in Russia in 1912 and immigrated to Canada in 1924; no Saskatchewan civil birth certificate can exist for him. External sites (eHealth Saskatchewan vital statistics, Library and Archives Canada homestead files, browse-only Saskatchewan provincial birth registration films) are outside autonomous FamilySearch session scope and documented as unsearched. No unsearched accessible source type is expected to name a different mother.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Who Was the Mother of Wendel Weichel?

**Research question:** Who was the mother of Wendel Weichel (FamilySearch ID G8Q5-BJ1), born 18 October 1912, died 27 December 1980, buried Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan?

**Conclusion (probable):** The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that Josephine Reiss Weichel (I1), born 7 September 1891 in Selz, near Odessa, then Russian Empire (now Ukraine), died 27 January 1974, buried Odessa, Saskatchewan, is the mother of Wendel Weichel. Her maiden name was Reiss.

---

### Sources and Evidence

**1. Canada Prairie Provinces Census, 1926 — the anchor record**

The 1926 Prairie Provinces Census records a household at Weyburn No. 67, Saskatchewan, headed by Jacob Weishel (b. 1890, Russia) with wife "Josefine Weishel" (b. 1892, Russia) and five children, the eldest named "Windelin Weichel" (b. 1913, Russia, male, single).^1 The census schedule explicitly records Windelin's relationship to the household head as child, and by the same column structure, to the wife as child — assertion a_035 is the direct parentage link.

This record is a derivative source (FamilySearch indexed transcript of the original census schedule); the original images are available at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C395-G92G-2. The relationship column was supplied by the census enumerator, making it primary information for household composition at the enumeration date. Informant proximity is *witness* (enumerator visiting the household). Information quality is *indeterminate* for names and birth data supplied by an unknown household member, but *primary* for the residence fact.

**Identification of Windelin Weichel as G8Q5-BJ1 (Wendel Weichel)**

The census child "Windelin Weichel" (b. 1913, Russia) is identified as the subject G8Q5-BJ1 (Wendel A. Weichel, b. 18 Oct 1912) at **probable** confidence (same-person score 0.64). The basis: (a) *Windelin*, *Wendelin*, and *Wendel* are established spelling variants of the same Germanic saint's name (Saint Wendelin); (b) surname Weichel is identical; (c) sex is male; (d) birthplace Russia is consistent; (e) the family's later burial at Odessa, Saskatchewan aligns precisely with G8Q5-BJ1's own burial at Odessa; (f) the 1-year birth year gap (census 1913, Find a Grave 1912) falls within normal census-rounding variation for ages reported orally to an enumerator. No alternative male Windelin/Wendel Weichel born c. 1912–1913 in Russia and resident in Weyburn-area Saskatchewan appeared in any searched record.

**2. Canada Immigration Records, 1919–1924 — corroborating origin and destination**

"Josephina Weichel" appears in the 1924 Canadian immigration records arriving from "Sely Near Odesea" — phonetic rendering of Selz, a Kutschurgan-area German Catholic colony near Odessa, then Russian Empire.^2 Her stated birth year (~1891) matches the Find a Grave birth date of 7 September 1891 precisely. She traveled with children born 1919, 1922, and 1923 (matching the younger Weishel children in the 1926 census: Peter b. 1919, Augina b. 1922, Katherina b. 1923) and stated destination *Odessa, Saskatchewan* (the indexed value "Wellburn, Ontario" is a transcription error confirmed by consulting the original manifest image at ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-C34W-PRCN, which reads "Odessa, Sask." with employer John Kleckner). This record is an original government manifest; Josephina is the informant for her own identity and origin (primary information for the enumeration date; secondary for birth facts). Evidence class: original source, primary/secondary information, direct evidence of identity and immigration.

Note: The manifest names Josephina's husband as "Joseph Weichel." This conflicts with the 1926 census head "Jacob Weishel" — see conflict resolution below.

**3. Find a Grave Index for Josephine Reiss Weichel — maiden name and burial**

The Find a Grave Index memorial for Josephine Reiss Weichel (FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:QVGH-T5TC, memorial no. 116369692) records: born 7 September 1891, died 27 January 1974, buried Odessa Cemetery, Regina Census Division, Saskatchewan.^3 The memorial name "Reiss Weichel" follows Find a Grave's maiden-name convention, encoding maiden surname REISS and married surname WEICHEL. She is buried in the same Odessa cemetery as Wendel A. Weichel (b. 18 Oct 1912, d. 27 Dec 1980), his wife Rose K. Deis Weichel, and their son Stanley Weichel (b. 1941) — a cohesive family burial cluster corroborating the mother-son relationship. This source is a derivative (volunteer-submitted memorial indexed by FamilySearch); informant is unknown; information quality is indeterminate. Its weight lies in the convergence of the maiden name with contextual placement at the same family burial ground.

---

### Conflict Resolution: Jacob vs. Joseph Weichel (c_001)

The 1924 immigration manifest names Josephina Weichel's husband as "Joseph Weichel," while the 1926 census names the household head "Jacob Weishel." This conflict (c_001) has been resolved in favor of Jacob on five grounds: (1) The 1926 Canadian census, taken two years after arrival by an enumerator visiting the household, is a stronger source than a Hamburg manifest completed by a Cunard shipping agent from oral information provided by Josephina, who could not read and could not verify the transcription; (2) A completely separate Joseph Weichel household (head b. 1882, wife Katherine b. 1884) was confirmed at Odessa, Francis No. 127 in the 1931 census — establishing that "Joseph Weichel" was a distinct, known community name the Hamburg agent could plausibly have substituted for "Jakob"; (3) "Jakob" and "Joseph" share the initial letter J and are both common Catholic German names — a phonetic or common-name substitution error by a German-speaking Hamburg agent is well-motivated; (4) The children's birth years and birth places on the manifest exactly match the children in the 1926 census household, confirming the records describe the same family despite the name discrepancy; (5) No candidate "Joseph Weichel" born c. 1890 with wife Josephina b. 1891 and the same set of children was found in any searched record.

---

### Source Classification Summary

| Source | Class | Information | Evidence | Weight |
|--------|-------|-------------|----------|--------|
| 1926 Prairie Provinces Census (src_004) | Derivative | Indeterminate (names/births); Primary (residence) | Direct (parentage relationship) | Moderate-high — direct parentage assertion; census enumerator as witness |
| Canada Immigration Records 1924 (src_003) | Original | Primary (identity/immigration); Secondary (birth year/place) | Direct (identity and origin) | Moderate-high — original government record; self-reported |
| Find a Grave — Josephine Reiss Weichel (src_002) | Derivative | Indeterminate | Direct (name, dates, burial) | Moderate — volunteer-submitted; maiden name REISS is a key finding requiring corroboration |
| Find a Grave — Wendel A. Weichel (src_001) | Derivative | Secondary | Direct (identity, burial) | Moderate — anchor for G8Q5-BJ1 identity; supports co-burial inference |

---

### Gaps and Limitations

The confidence tier is **probable**, not proved, for two reasons. First, the Windelin Weichel = Wendel Weichel identification carries a probable (not confident) match score of 0.64, meaning the parentage chain from Josefine to G8Q5-BJ1 is mediated by an inference. Second, the decisive original record — the Catholic baptism register from Selz (Kutschurgan colony), which would name both parents — is held in European church archives and was not accessible through North American FamilySearch-based tools during this research session. No Saskatchewan civil birth certificate exists for Wendel because he was born in 1912 in Russia and immigrated to Canada only in 1924. The maiden name REISS, established only through the Find a Grave memorial, has not been independently corroborated from a primary source. Three independent Canadian records from three distinct institutions agree on the identity of the mother; no alternative candidate has appeared in any searched record.

**To advance to proved:** Locate and examine the Selz (Odessa colony) Catholic baptismal register for an entry for Wendelin/Wendel Weichel, born c. 18 October 1912, naming both parents. The registers for Kutschurgan-area colonies are held at the Odessa Oblast State Archive (Odessa, Ukraine) and are partially microfilmed through FamilySearch (collection 8038568, "Ukraine, Odessa Oblast, Civil and Church Records"). Additionally, a Saskatchewan provincial birth registration for Wendel, if one was filed (unlikely for a child born in Russia), could be ordered from eHealth Saskatchewan Vital Statistics.

---

^1 "Canada, Prairie Provinces, Census, 1926," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:QTM1-JBYT : accessed 9 September 2026), entry for Jacob Weishel and Josefine Weishel, Weyburn No. 67, Saskatchewan.

^2 "Canada, Immigration Records, 1919-1924," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6ZBB-N884 : accessed 9 September 2026), entry for Josephina Weichel, 1924.

^3 "Find a Grave Index," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QVGH-T5TC : accessed 9 September 2026), entry for Josephine Reiss Weichel; citing Find a Grave memorial no. 116369692.

quirks: Civil registration of births and deaths began at the provincial level in 1888, but implementation was slow — many registrations were not recorded until approximately 1920. A 1912 birth may or may not have a registered certificate; check eHealth Saskatchewan first, then supplement with census and church records.

Birth records >100 years old are now publicly accessible (Wendel's 1912 birth qualifies). Order a genealogical copy from eHealth Saskatchewan Vital Statistics (101-1445 Park Street, Regina, SK S4N 4C5; genealogy.ehealthsask.ca). From 1889 the form names father and maiden name of mother; from 1898 birthplace of parents; from 1916 age of parents and parents' marriage date — making the 1912 registration form highly informative if it was filed.

The key FamilySearch collection 'Canada, Saskatchewan Provincial Records, 1879-1987' (collection 1916143, 1,506,449 images) is BROWSE-ONLY — 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable. Must be browsed image by image. Use the eHealth Saskatchewan index (genealogy.ehealthsask.ca) to identify the registration number first, then locate the image in this collection.

Saskatchewan was part of the Northwest Territories before September 1905. All events before that date were recorded under NWT jurisdiction. Odessa village dates from 1905, so this is rarely relevant for our 1912-era subject.

The Weichel surname is German in origin. German-speaking settlers in southeastern Saskatchewan (Francis No. 127 area) were predominantly Lutheran or Catholic. Check FamilySearch collection 2001071 (Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records, 1846-1957 — indexed) and contact the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Canada Saskatchewan Synod (Saskatoon, info@sasksynod.ca) for baptism registers. The Provincial Archives of Saskatchewan (Regina) holds United, Anglican, and Presbyterian registers on microfilm.

Census records are the most immediately searchable source: 1911 (FS collection 2143998), 1916 Prairie Provinces (FS 1529118), 1921 (FS 5000285), 1926 Prairie Provinces (FS 3005862), 1931 (FS 5000196) — all indexed and searchable by name. A child born 1912 would appear in the 1916 census at ~age 4 (in parents' household), 1921 at ~age 9, 1926 at ~age 14, and 1931 at ~age 19. Each census names head of household and relationship; 1921 onward typically names parents for minor children.

Homestead land grants (Ancestry collection 9209, Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta Homestead Grant Registers, 1872-1930) and the Saskatchewan Homestead Index (saskhomesteads.com) can identify the father's land entry and sometimes household composition — useful for placing the family geographically.

Neighboring municipalities to Francis No. 127 were not returned by FamilySearch Wiki tools; consult the RM of Francis No. 127 municipal records or the Saskatchewan Archives for neighbor-municipality names. Families often had records on both sides of municipal boundaries.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan, Canada (1900–1940)

**Standard place (FamilySearch):** Odessa, Francis No. 127, Saskatchewan, Canada (village, est. 1905)

## Jurisdictional History

Odessa village was established in 1905, the same year Saskatchewan became a province (formerly part of the Northwest Territories). All records from 1905 onward fall under Saskatchewan provincial jurisdiction. There are no earlier records under the Odessa place name.

## Record Types and Availability

### 1. Civil Vital Registration (Births, Marriages, Deaths)

**Registration began:** Marriages from 1878 (provincial); births and deaths from 1888 (provincial). Many registrations not actually filed until ~1920 due to implementation difficulties.

**Birth registration contents:**
- 1889+: Name, date, place, sex, name of father, **maiden name of mother** ← key field for q_001
- 1898+: Birthplace of parents
- 1916+: Age of parents, number of children born to date, date and place of parents' marriage

A 1912 birth registration for Wendel Weichel, if filed, would name his mother's maiden name directly.

**Access:**
- **Index:** eHealth Saskatchewan: http://genealogy.ehealthsask.ca/vsgs_srch.aspx (free)
- **Index (paid):** MyHeritage — Canada, Saskatchewan Births, 1832-1921; Findmypast — Saskatchewan Vital Records Birth Index; Ancestry — Saskatchewan Birth Index 1875-1908 (too early for 1912 birth)
- **Images:** FamilySearch — Canada, Saskatchewan Provincial Records, 1879-1987 (collection 1916143); **BROWSE-ONLY** — 1,506,449 images, 0% indexed. Use eHealth index to get registration number first.
- **Certified copies:** Order from eHealth Saskatchewan Vital Statistics, 101-1445 Park Street, Regina, SK S4N 4C5; phone 1-855-347-5465; VitalStatistics@ehealthsask.ca

### 2. Census Records ← Primary parallel source

All major censuses are name-indexed and searchable at FamilySearch (free):

| Census | FamilySearch Collection | Notes |
|--------|------------------------|-------|
| 1906 NW Provinces | 1584925 | Index only |
| 1911 Canada | 2143998 | Index + images |
| 1916 Prairie Provinces | 1529118 | Index + images |
| 1921 Canada | 5000285 | Index + images |
| 1926 Prairie Provinces | 3005862 | Index + images |
| 1931 Canada | 5000196 | Index + images |

Wendel (b. 1912) would appear as a child in the 1916 census (~age 4), 1921 (~age 9), and 1926 (~age 14) in his parents' household. Each of these censuses names household members and relationships, giving the parents' names directly.

### 3. Church Records

German surname Weichel suggests Lutheran or Catholic community.

**Catholic (indexed, most accessible):**
- FamilySearch collection 2001071 — Canada, Saskatchewan Catholic Church Records, 1846-1957 (40,494 records, 120,185 persons) — **indexed + images**
- Ancestry — Saskatchewan Catholic Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1867-1932 (index + images, $)
- Archdiocese of Regina Archives: 2522 Retallack St, Regina, SK S4T 2L3 (baptismal records by parish)

**Lutheran:**
- FamilySearch Catalog: search under 'Canada, Saskatchewan' → town of Odessa → Church records
- Evangelical Lutheran Church in Canada Saskatchewan Synod: #6–2220 Northridge Drive, Saskatoon; info@sasksynod.ca; 306-244-2474
- Lutheran Theological Seminary Saskatoon: 114 Seminary Crescent, Saskatoon SK S7N 0X3; 306-966-7850

**United/Anglican/Presbyterian:**
- Provincial Archives of Saskatchewan (Regina): holds United, Anglican, and Presbyterian microfilm registers
- United Church of Canada Living Skies Region Archives: livingskiesarchives@united-church.ca (holds pre-1925 Methodist, Presbyterian, Congregational records)
- Anglican Diocese of Qu'Appelle Archives: 1501 College Avenue, Regina, SK S4P 1B8; 306-585-0390

### 4. Land and Homestead Records

- **Ancestry** — Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta, Canada, Homestead Grant Registers, 1872-1930 (collection 9209; index + images, $)
- **SaskHomesteads.com** — Saskatchewan Homestead Index (free; searchable by name)
- FamilySearch — Saskatchewan Provincial Records, 1879-1987 (collection 1916143; browse-only)

Father's homestead entry may show date of settlement, legal land description, and sometimes family composition.

### 5. Cemetery and Burial Records

- FamilySearch — Canada, Saskatchewan Cemetery Transcripts, ca. 1850-1994 (collection 2258205; 164,737 records; **indexed + images**)
- Ancestry — Saskatchewan, Canada, Cemetery Transcripts, 1850-1994 (collection 61500, $)
- Saskatchewan Burial Index, 1802-2011 at Ancestry (collection 8841; index only, $)
- Saskatchewan Genealogical Society Burial Index: http://saskgenealogy.com/databases/burials/
- Find a Grave and BillionGraves: searchable for Saskatchewan cemeteries

### 6. Probate Records

- FamilySearch — Canada, Saskatchewan Probate Estate Files, 1887-1931 (collection 1918293; 41,130 records; **indexed + images**)

If either parent died before 1931, a probate file may name surviving spouse, children, and their relationships.

### 7. Newspapers

- Saskatchewan Historic Newspapers Online: http://sabnewspapers.usask.ca/ (1884-2000)
- Saskatchewan News Index at University of Saskatchewan: http://library2.usask.ca/sni/ (1884-2000)
